commitResults.messageTitle: Update README and site settings for TutorFlow
commitResults.messageBody:
The README, homepage and navigation bar still described the
AddressBook-Level3 sample project, so the project website did not
match the product the team is building.

Rewrite the README and homepage to describe TutorFlow and credit
AddressBook-Level3 as the original source. Replace docs/images/Ui.png
with a mockup of the intended TutorFlow window, kept at the same
726 x 593 size as the original so the layout is unchanged. Rename the
navigation bar brand from AB-3 to TutorFlow and point its GitHub link
at the team repository.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TutorFlow requirements to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Requirements appendix still held the AddressBook-Level3 sample
content, so the Developer Guide did not describe who TutorFlow is for
or what it must do.

Replace the product scope, user stories, use cases, non-functional
requirements and glossary with TutorFlow content taken from the team's
project notes. The sections cover the full intended product, including
homework and payment tracking, rather than only the features planned
for the next iteration, so that every identified requirement is
recorded for later iterations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lower homework and payment story priorities
commitResults.messageBody:
Homework and payment tracking were marked as high priority, but the
team has decided to treat them as nice to have so that the must-have
set stays focused on student records, scheduling and the dashboard.

Change the seven homework and payment user stories that were high
priority to medium priority.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sort command to order persons by name
commitResults.messageBody:
Persons are listed in the order they were added, so a tutor with many
contacts has no quick way to scan them alphabetically.

Add a sort command that orders all persons by name, ignoring letter
case, in ascending order by default or descending order with the desc
argument. The sorted order is kept in the address book so that it is
saved and shown again on the next launch, and the command shows all
persons so a filtered list does not hide the result.

Add sortPersons to Model, ModelManager, AddressBook and
UniquePersonList to support the command. Add tests for the command,
its parser and the new model methods, and document the command in the
User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add level, subject, rate and venue value objects
commitResults.messageBody:
TutorFlow needs to record who a student is and what they are taught,
but the address book only has name, phone, email, address and tags
fields, none of which describe a student's level, subjects, rate or
usual venue.

Add Level, Subject, Rate and Venue as validated, immutable value
objects in the same style as the existing Name and Phone classes.
Levels are P1-P6, S1-S5 and J1-J2. Subjects are short free text that is
compared ignoring case. Rates are 0 to 9999.99 dollars with up to two
decimal places. Venues are 1-100 characters of free text.

The classes are not used yet, so behavior is unchanged. They are tested
on their own so that the commit passes the existing checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace address and tags with student details in Person
commitResults.messageBody:
A Person only holds contact details, an address and tags, so TutorFlow
cannot yet record what a tutor needs to know about a student: their
level, the subjects taught, the lesson rate or the usual venue. Teammates
cannot start on lessons, payments or filtering until these exist.

Give Person a level, a set of subjects, a rate and an optional venue,
and make the email optional, as a tutor often only has a phone number.
Remove the address and tags, which nothing else uses, together with the
Address and Tag classes. A single Person class is used rather than a
Student subclass, so that no code needs to cast between the two.

Two persons now count as the same when they share a phone number and a
name that matches ignoring case, instead of the name alone, because
unrelated students can share a name. Optional values are returned as
Optional so that callers cannot forget to handle a missing one.

Update the add and edit commands, the Jackson storage, the sample data
and the person card to match. Existing remark and sort behavior is
unchanged. The tests are updated and extended to cover the new fields.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use student wording in command messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and edit usage messages now talk about students, but the
success, error and help messages of the other commands still say
person, which reads as two different products to a tutor.

Change the user-facing text of the add, edit, delete, list, find,
remark and sort commands, and of the invalid index and listed count
messages, to say student. Only the text changes. The constants keep
their names and the behavior is the same.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student details in the guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide still described adding and editing a person with an
address and tags, and the Developer Guide model diagram still showed
those classes, so both disagreed with the product.

Describe the add and edit formats with the level, subjects, rate, venue
and optional email, with the rules for each value and for duplicate
students. Update the quick start examples and the command summary. In
the Developer Guide, redraw the model diagram with the new value
objects, describe a Person as a student, and remove the note and the
diagram about the alternative design for tags, which no longer exist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #39 from joshmode/add-student-fields
Allow common punctuation in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names such as "Priya s/o Kumar", "O'Brien-Smith Jr." or
"Tan Wei Ming (twin A)" were rejected because only letters, digits and
spaces were accepted. The feature specification expects names to permit
the punctuation needed to tell students apart, and rejecting real names
is the kind of over-strict validation users trip over.

A name must still start with a letter or digit so that a blank or
punctuation-only name stays invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add lesson date, time, duration and status types
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson needs validated values for when it happens and how long it
runs. Dates accept ISO (2026-09-22) and d/M/yyyy, times accept 24-hour
and 12-hour forms, and durations are 15 to 480 minutes in steps of 15.
The status distinguishes scheduled, completed, cancelled and missed
lessons so that only scheduled lessons take part in conflict checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Lesson and a unique lesson list
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson links a student, identified by name and phone number, to a
subject, date, time, duration and optional venue. It rejects a slot
that runs past midnight and reports whether it overlaps another
scheduled lesson on the same date by at least one minute, so that
back-to-back lessons are not flagged.

Person gains hasIdentity so that lessons and persons share a single
definition of who a student is. UniqueLessonList rejects lessons that
share student, subject, date, time and duration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store lessons in the address book and model
commitResults.messageBody:
The address book now owns a list of lessons next to its persons, and
the model exposes add, delete, replace and conflict lookups plus a
filtered lesson list for the agenda to show.

Lessons belong to a student, so deleting a student also removes their
lessons, and editing the name or phone number of a student keeps their
lessons attached instead of leaving them orphaned.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save and load lessons in the JSON data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Lessons are written next to the students in the data file. A data file
without a lesson list still loads, so files written before lessons
existed keep working. Field conversion in JsonAdaptedLesson shares one
helper that checks presence and validity, so each field is handled the
same way and a bad value reports the matching constraint message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support rescheduling, cancelling and ordering lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
Moving a lesson keeps its student, subject and status, and cancelling
keeps the whole record with its reason, so a cancelled slot is still
known when a fee is disputed. A lesson can also tell whether it is
still upcoming and format its time range.

The model now shows lessons in agenda order (date, start time, then
student name), so the index a user sees in the agenda is the index the
lesson commands act on. Overlap lookups no longer report a lesson as
overlapping itself, which a reschedule would otherwise trip over.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parsing helpers for lesson commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The lesson commands share a few argument shapes: dates, times and
durations, a reason for cancelling, flags such as week/ that take no
value, and a check that every required prefix is present. Putting them
in ParserUtil lets each command parser stay a few lines long.

A missing prefix now lists exactly which parameters are missing, so a
tutor typing quickly can see what to add. Flags reject a value, so
"week/yes" is reported instead of being silently accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson add command
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson add st/INDEX d/DATE t/TIME" schedules a lesson for a student
in the displayed student list. To keep typing short, the subject can
be left out when the student takes only one, the duration defaults to
60 minutes and the venue defaults to the student's venue.

A subject the student does not take, a past date, a date more than two
years ahead, a lesson that would run past midnight and an exact
duplicate are rejected with a message that says what to fix. An overlap
with another scheduled lesson only warns, because a tutor may double
book on purpose, and back-to-back lessons are not an overlap.

Lesson commands share the "lesson" command word, which a new
LessonCommandParser dispatches to the right parser.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson list and agenda commands
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson list st/INDEX" shows a student's upcoming lessons, or all of
them including past and cancelled ones with "all/". "agenda" shows
today's lessons, "agenda d/DATE" a given day and "agenda week/" the
Monday to Sunday week containing the day. Both set the lesson list
that is currently shown, so the number next to a lesson is the index
that the lesson commands take.

The agenda marks lessons that overlap another one, keeps cancelled
lessons visible but leaves them out of the count and total time, and
says so when a day has no lessons instead of failing. A flag such as
"week/yes" that should not take a value is reported.

The shared student lookup moves into LessonCommandUtil so that lesson
add and lesson list use the same index check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share optional-value parsing between lesson parsers
commitResults.messageBody:
Lesson add and the upcoming lesson move both read several optional
values, each of which was a four-line "if present then parse" block.
ParserUtil.parseOptional returns the parsed value or null, which keeps
each parser short and handles every optional value the same way.

LessonCommandUtil also gains the lesson index lookup and the past-date
check, so that lesson add no longer carries its own copy of the check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson move and lesson cancel commands
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson move INDEX" reschedules the lesson at that index in the lesson
list that is currently shown. Only the given date, time, duration and
venue change, so the tutor does not re-enter the student or subject.
A move that creates an overlap still succeeds with a warning, while a
completed or cancelled lesson, a past or very distant new date, a slot
past midnight and a move onto an identical lesson are rejected.

"lesson cancel INDEX [r/REASON]" keeps the lesson in the agenda marked
as cancelled with its reason, so that the record of the booking is
kept for billing. A cancelled lesson no longer counts as an overlap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the lesson commands in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Describes lesson add, agenda, lesson list, lesson move and lesson cancel
with their formats, defaults, limits and examples, and adds them to the
command summary. The format notes now explain flags such as week/ that
take no value, and use parameters that exist in TutorFlow instead of the
leftover AB3 t/TAG example. The add section states which punctuation a
student name may contain.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document lesson scheduling in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds an implementation section for lesson scheduling, the agenda and
overlap detection, with a sequence diagram for lesson move and the
design alternatives considered for how a lesson refers to its student
and for what to do when lessons overlap. The model and storage
components and the model class diagram now include lessons, and the
manual testing section gets test cases for the lesson commands.
